title: Recognizing Dialogue Ambiguity via Candidate Set Visual Grounding
abstract: arXiv:2610.19723v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Interpreting an ambiguous utterance in real-world interactions often requires context beyond a single utterance. When the utterance refers to objects in a visual scene, it is necessary to maintain and update the set of plausible referents as context accumulates, without assuming that the available information identifies a unique object. However, prior work on interactive visual grounding, which localizes objects referred to by linguistic expressions, has focused on identifying a unique object once sufficient dialogue context becomes available. To address this gap, we propose Candidate Set Visual Grounding (CSVG), a task for estimating the set of objects consistent with the given dialogue context. We further introduce CandVG, a benchmark that evaluates how the candidate set changes across dialogue turns. translated_title: 通过候选集视觉定位识别对话歧义
translated_abstract: 在真实世界的交互中，解读一句有歧义的话语往往需要超出单句话语的上下文信息。当话语指向视觉场景中的物体时，需要随着上下文的积累不断维护和更新可能指代对象的集合，而不能假设已有信息能够唯一确定某个物体。然而，以往关于交互式视觉定位（即根据语言表达定位所指物体）的研究，主要聚焦于在获得足够的对话上下文后识别出唯一的物体。为填补这一空白，我们提出了候选集视觉定位，这是一项估计与给定对话上下文一致的物体集合的任务。我们进一步推出了 CandVG 基准，用于评估候选集如何随对话轮次变化而变化。我们对视觉-语言模型的评估表明，更强的视觉定位能力并不一定会带来更好的 CSVG 表现。
tldr: 该论文提出了候选集视觉定位（CSVG）这一新任务及 CandVG 基准，通过估计与对话上下文一致的目标物体集合来识别对话歧义，并发现更强的视觉定位能力并不一定带来更好的 CSVG 表现。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Candidate Set Visual Grounding (CSVG), a new task of estimating the set of objects consistent with dialogue context to recognize dialogue ambiguity, along with the CandVG benchmark, showing that stronger visual grounding capability does not necessarily yield better CSVG performance.
